title: Update Airtable Expense via Uploaded Audio
hard_category_focus: Airtable as CRM for project tracking
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing the full public product path for an audio-upload expense update in a signed-in Airtable CRM surface, requiring the engine to handle a real-world operations task with a decline path when surface proof fails.

v7_target.surface_rule: user must be signed in to Chrome profile with Airtable access and Airtable dashboard visible with base list
v7_target.proof_rule: fresh screenshot or DOM capture of the Airtable record before and after change, tied to the public build that produced it

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage is the primary input path to test the engine's ability to process a user-recorded mp3 file through /api/listen/upload, avoiding live mic or transcript paste which would bypass the audio upload proof path.

real_user_surfaces.name: Airtable signed-in Chrome profile
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible Airtable dashboard with base list and signed-in user indicator

real_user_surfaces.name: Airtable Expenses base record
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: visible record for Brookline coffee charge with category field

moments.description: Driver navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, signs in, completes onboarding, downloads the public installer, and installs the user-device engine on their computer.
Driver verifies that the user is signed into Chrome with the Airtable profile, and that the Airtable dashboard is visible with the Expenses base listed.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please update the Airtable Expenses record for the Brookline coffee charge from yesterday and tag it work meetings. If you cannot prove the visible Airtable record or my signed-in workspace, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger will record this text as an mp3 file using a local audio tool, then upload the file via the /api/listen/upload endpoint. The audio file must be a fresh recording per run; no pre-recorded or cached files allowed.

moments.description: Engine confirms that the ASR output matches the spoken reference text and that the user's signed-in Airtable surface is still visible in the same Chrome profile.

acceptable_outcomes.condition: Airtable record is visible and editable; engine updates the category field to 'work meetings' and provides a fresh proof screenshot.
Airtable record is visible but category field is locked or requires confirmation; engine asks user for explicit confirmation before making the change.
Airtable record or signed-in workspace is not provably visible; engine declines without making any changes and explains why.

moments.description: Driver notes that the primary input was audio upload; no secondary input mode (transcript paste or live mic) was used, confirming the audio upload path is the sole input channel for this script.

success_criteria: The engine processes the uploaded mp3 audio through /api/listen/upload and accurately transcribes the spoken request.
The engine verifies the user's signed-in Airtable surface in the same Chrome profile before taking any action.
If the Airtable record is visible and editable, the engine updates the category field to 'work meetings' and provides a fresh proof screenshot of the changed record.
If the Airtable record or workspace is not provably visible, the engine declines without making any changes and provides a clear reason.
The entire script completes without using any fake receipts, stale proofs, cloned Chrome profiles, or mocked API responses.
failure_triggers: The engine uses a pre-recorded or cached audio file instead of a fresh per-run recording.
The engine attempts to update the Airtable record without first proving the user's signed-in workspace is visible.
The engine provides a proof screenshot from a different session or browser profile than the one the user is currently using.
The engine falls back to transcript paste or live mic input instead of processing the uploaded audio file.
The engine makes a change to the Airtable record when the surface is not provably visible, violating the decline condition.
